Apply a shared fold table to any nested data

Source: R/apply_folds.R
apply_folds.Rd

apply_folds() turns a nested table (from w2l_nest(), c2p_nest(), r2p_nest() or built by hand) into training / validation sets using a fold table from cv_folds(). Rows are matched to folds through the individual ID, so single-trait, multi-trait and across-group models all get identical validation individuals.

Nested rows that differ only in the grouping column(s) of the fold table (e.g. w2l_nest(..., by = "herd")) are merged first, and the grouping column is put back inside the data (right after the ID column), so the training set of every scenario carries the group as a possible fixed effect.

apply_folds(data, folds, ref = "none", out_type = "dt")

Arguments

data

A nested data.table / data.frame (a list-column named data, or the first data.frame list-column, is used), or a plain table.

folds

A fold table from cv_folds().

ref

"none": train on the target group only. "others": also add all records of the other groups to every training set (reference population enlarged by the other groups; they are never validated).

out_type

"dt" (default) or "df" for the nested subsets.

Value

A data.table with the outer columns of data, the grouping column(s) of folds (the validated group), rep, fold, and the list-columns train and validate.

See also

cv_folds(), cv_scenarios()

Examples

dat <- data.frame(id = paste0("i", 1:40), herd = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20),
                  adg = rnorm(40), bf = rnorm(40))
folds <- cv_folds(dat, id = "id", by = "herd", v = 5, seed = 1)
# single-trait, within herd
apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf"), by = "herd"), folds)
#>       name   herd     rep   fold              train          validate
#>     <char> <char>  <char> <char>             <list>            <list>
#>  1:    adg      A Repeat1  Fold1 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  2:    adg      A Repeat1  Fold2 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  3:    adg      A Repeat1  Fold3 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  4:    adg      A Repeat1  Fold4 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  5:    adg      A Repeat1  Fold5 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  6:    adg      B Repeat1  Fold1 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  7:    adg      B Repeat1  Fold2 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  8:    adg      B Repeat1  Fold3 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>  9:    adg      B Repeat1  Fold4 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 10:    adg      B Repeat1  Fold5 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 11:     bf      A Repeat1  Fold1 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 12:     bf      A Repeat1  Fold2 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 13:     bf      A Repeat1  Fold3 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 14:     bf      A Repeat1  Fold4 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 15:     bf      A Repeat1  Fold5 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 16:     bf      B Repeat1  Fold1 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 17:     bf      B Repeat1  Fold2 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 18:     bf      B Repeat1  Fold3 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 19:     bf      B Repeat1  Fold4 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#> 20:     bf      B Repeat1  Fold5 <data.table[16x3]> <data.table[4x3]>
#>       name   herd     rep   fold              train          validate
#>     <char> <char>  <char> <char>             <list>            <list>
# single-trait, other herd added to the training set
apply_folds(w2l_nest(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf")), folds, ref = "others")
#>       name   herd     rep   fold              train          validate
#>     <char> <char>  <char> <char>             <list>            <list>
